A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GiG research, with matching architecture, benchmarks, and extensive retained results. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices, including the graphical prompts in v1, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on Robotouille Synchronous, Robotouille Asynchronous, and ALFWorld, alongside component ablations, embedding analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical evaluations and adds ExpeL comparisons, observation-noise experiments, an experience-only ablation, and context-token measurements.

M1.justification: The graph architecture, losses, retrieval rule, and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged. However, the specified action-generation prompt changes: v3 Appendix D adds cutting restrictions and explicit delayed-action interleaving instructions, and removes v1's requirement that Summary include the following planned step. These are limited changes to documented inference instructions.

E1.justification: The three benchmarks and their underlying task coverage remain unchanged. Section 4.8 adds evaluation with randomly inserted or omitted observation items, extending coverage to corrupted-input scenarios without introducing another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: ExpeL is added to the ALFWorld comparison across Qwen3, DeepSeek, and Gemini, with aggregate and per-task results in v3 Tables 3 and 17–19. ReCAP and ReAct remain; the Robotouille comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include observation corruption every five or ten steps, an experience-only ablation control, and measurement of average prefill tokens per step. Core task counts, Pass@1 evaluation, decoding budgets, and Robotouille step caps remain unchanged. The supplied Robotouille prompt is revised, but the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through perception-noise testing, an experience-only ablation, and empirical context-consumption comparisons (Sections 4.8–4.9). The full-system 97% result already existed in v1; its inclusion in the expanded ablation is consolidation. Likewise, the combined appendix embedding plots reuse existing analyses.

E5.justification: v3 newly identifies the training environment seed as the source for memory and GNN-training trajectories (Section 4.1; Appendix B.2). Ten-run Robotouille evaluations and existing step-variability reporting are retained. Table 7 extends mean-and-standard-deviation reporting to context consumption, without establishing additional repetitions or a new statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Most existing benchmark aggregates remain unchanged, but substantial results are added: ExpeL scores 91/75/89 on ALFWorld for Qwen3/DeepSeek/Gemini; experience-only planning scores 95%; and Table 5 reports GiG at 93/94/93 versus ReAct at 74/67/62 for clean, ten-step-noise, and five-step-noise conditions. Table 7 adds average context usage of 12,297/40,720/57,357 tokens for GiG/ReCAP/ReAct. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, training objective, retrieval equations, and attention-cost derivation remain substantively unchanged. Renaming the triplet margin from alpha to gamma and moving the cost analysis from Appendix A.3 to C.6 do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central graph-memory and planning-efficiency contributions remain. The abstract changes the synchronous headline advantage from 22 to 19 percentage points, consistent with comparing 93 against the strongest baseline's 74. The introduction adds perception-noise robustness, and the conclusion gives greater prominence to model-independent experience transfer.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations attributing noise robustness to persistent graph updates and planning quality primarily to retrieved experience. It explicitly distinguishes in-domain compositional transfer from unresolved out-of-domain transfer and restricts applicability to symbolic planning rather than physical control. Appendix B.1 also qualifies v1's strong embedding-separation interpretation by acknowledging blurred boundaries for longer asynchronous trajectories.

D1.justification: v3 specifies that the 50 successful memory trajectories come from Qwen3-235B across all ten task types using the training environment seed, and clarifies GNN-training provenance. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit ALFWorld 50-step episode limit and the statement that GNN training includes successful and failed trajectories. These are documentation changes, not established changes to the underlying settings.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds EvoMem and ExpeL, broadening comparison with specialized memory architectures and experience-based agents. New citations to Ichter et al. and Liu et al. help distinguish symbolic planning from physical execution. The principal positioning relative to graph retrieval, ReAct, and ReCAP remains.

P1.justification: v3 extensively edits existing prose and reorganizes the appendices into benchmark descriptions, GNN details, grouped experimental results, and prompts. It substantially rewrites the limitations and several experimental discussions, adds an impact statement, and corrects the title. This is a substantial editorial and structural revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds noise and context-consumption tables, expands ablation and ALFWorld displays, adds gain annotations, and redraws Figure 6 with ExpeL. It relocates the overview figure, combines existing embedding plots, reorganizes appendix tables, and replaces two prompt figures with a multipage text listing. These are substantial display changes, including redistribution of retained content.

improvement.justification: The experience-only control, ExpeL comparison, and measured context consumption strengthen evidence for the central memory and efficiency claims; noise testing and clearer transfer limits also improve assessment. Reporting defects limit the gain: v3 drops the ALFWorld step-cap disclosure, Table 4 labels gains over GiG as gains over the best baseline, and Appendix D's cutting restriction conflicts with onion-cutting tasks. The added evidence supports a limited net improvement despite these documentation problems.
